What is Angular? A Beginner's Introducti: Angular = a framework from Google for building web apps in TypeScript.
You build the screen from components: a class, a template and styles.
Routing, forms, HTTP and testing tools come in one place.
When data changes, Angular updates only the parts of the page that need it.
TypeScript Basics for Angular: TypeScript = JavaScript with types. You say what kind of value a variable or function holds.
The editor and compiler check types while you type, so mistakes show up early.
Most used in Angular: interfaces, classes and decorators.
It is turned into plain JavaScript for the browser.
Install Node.js and the Angular CLI: Install Node.js first. Angular tools run on it.
npm comes with Node and installs packages.
Angular Course Roadmap and Complete Topi: Path: basics, then state and forms, then routing and HTTP, then advanced topics, then projects and deploy.
State = signals and services. Real data = routing and HTTP.
Advanced = RxJS, change detection, SSR, testing, security.
Create Your First Angular App with the C: `ng new my-app` creates a complete project.
`cd my-app` then `ng serve` starts the dev server.
Save a file and the browser reloads by itself.
Angular Project Structure Explained: `main.ts` is the entry point and starts the app.
The root component holds the page layout.
`app.routes.ts` says which component shows for each URL.
Everything is drawn inside `index.html`, the one page the browser loads.
Your First Angular Component: A component = a class with a `@Component` decorator.
The template is HTML that shows data from the class. Styles apply only to this component.
`selector` is the custom tag name, for example `<app-card>`.
Put the tag in another template and Angular draws the component there.
Make one with `ng generate component name`.
Angular CLI Guide: ng new, ng update, Mu: The Angular CLI is one tool for the whole life of a project.
`ng new` creates, `ng serve` runs, `ng build` makes the files to deploy.
`ng generate` makes components, services and more with the right files.
`ng update` upgrades Angular and runs migrations on your code.
Upgrade one major version at a time.
Displaying Data in Angular with Interpol: Interpolation: `{{ title }}` shows a class property in the template.
When the property changes, the text updates.
Small expressions work inside the braces, such as `{{ price * 2 }}`.
Keep logic short in templates. Move bigger logic to the class.
Property Binding and Event Binding in An: Property binding: `[disabled]="isBusy"` sets an element property from the class.
Event binding: `(click)="save()"` runs a method when the event happens.
Square brackets = data in. Round brackets = events out.
The method changes the data and the bindings update the screen.
Angular Two-Way Binding: ngModel, ngMode: Two-way binding keeps a property and an input in sync in both directions.
Anything else that shows `name` updates as the user types.
Angular Signals: Reactive State for Begi: A signal holds a value and tells Angular when it changes.
Angular knows which parts of the page read the signal and refreshes only those.
Update signals with new objects and arrays, not by changing them in place.
Angular Styling: Global Styles, Componen: `styles.css` = global styles for the whole app.
Component styles apply only to that component.
View encapsulation is how Angular stops a component's styles leaking out.
Libraries such as Bootstrap and Font Awesome are added once and used through classes.
Conditional Rendering in Angular with @i: `@if (cond) { ... } @else { ... }` decides which blocks exist on the page.
Only the matching block is added. The other is not in the page at all.
Control flow is built in. No import is needed.
Rendering Lists in Angular with @for and: `@for (item of items; track item.id) { ... }` repeats a block for each item.
`track` tells Angular which item is which. Use a unique id.
Angular then adds, moves or removes only what changed.
`@empty { ... }` shows something when the list is empty.
Angular ngIf, ngFor, ngSwitch and trackB: Older code uses `*ngIf`, `*ngFor`, `*ngSwitch` and `trackBy`. You will still meet them.
The new `@if`, `@for` and `@switch` do the same job with less code.
A built-in migration converts templates for you: `ng generate @angular/core:control-flow`.
Review the changes and run your tests.
Angular ngClass, ngStyle, Class Binding: A class binding adds or removes one class: `[class.active]="isActive"`.
`ngClass` handles several classes from an object or a list.
A style binding sets one property: `[style.width.px]="size"`.
The element updates whenever the state changes.
Computed Signals and Effects in Angular: `computed(() => price() * qty())` calculates a value from other signals.
It recalculates only when those signals change, and is cached until then.
`effect(() => ...)` runs code when the signals it reads change.
Use effects for logging or saving to storage, not to calculate values.
Signals in Practice: Build a Shopping Ca: The cart keeps its lines in one signal.
Item count and total are `computed` signals that read the lines.
The cart view refreshes with no extra code.
Angular Component Inputs: Pass Data to C: A parent gives data to a child with an input: `[product]="item"`.
In the child: `product = input.required<Product>()`. Read it with `product()`.
Data flows one way, from parent to child.
When the parent value changes, the child updates.
Angular Component Outputs and Two-Way Bi: A child tells its parent with an output: `saved = output<string>()`, then `saved.emit(value)`.
`model()` combines an input and an output, so the child can change a value the parent owns.
Angular Pipes: Format Dates, Currency an: A pipe changes how a value is shown, not the value itself.
`{{ value | pipeName }}`. Add options with a colon: `date:'dd MMM yyyy'`.
Angular Built-in Pipes: Date, Async, Key: The `async` pipe subscribes to an observable or promise and shows its latest value.
It unsubscribes when the component is destroyed, so you cannot forget.
`keyvalue` loops over the keys and values of an object.
In TypeScript, inject the pipe or create it and call `transform`.
Angular Lifecycle Hooks: OnInit, OnDestr: A component is created, updates, then is removed. Hooks let you run code at each stage.
`ngOnInit` runs once after inputs are set: load initial data here.
`ngAfterViewInit` runs once the view and children exist.
`ngOnDestroy` runs just before removal: stop timers and subscriptions.
Template Reference Variables, ng-contain: `#box` gives a name to an element in the template.
`viewChild()` gets something inside the component's own template.
`contentChild()` gets something the parent projected in.
`ng-container` groups elements or holds an `@if` without adding an extra element.
Angular Services and Dependency Injectio: A service = a class that holds logic or data you want to reuse, such as API calls.
A component asks for it with `inject(MyService)`. It does not use `new`.
Every component gets the same instance.
Components stay small and services are easy to replace in tests.
Share State Between Components with an A: Two unrelated components that need the same data: put the data in a service.
The service is one shared instance and keeps the state in a signal.
Component A calls a service method to change it.
Component B reads the signal and updates by itself.
Angular Hierarchical Dependency Injectio: Angular has a tree of injectors that follows the component tree.
A request looks in the component's own providers, then the parent, then the root.
A provider on a component gives that branch its own instance.
`@Self` = only here. `@SkipSelf` = start at the parent. `@Optional` = no error if missing. `@Host` = stop at the host.
Angular Reactive Forms for Beginners: Reactive form: you build the model in the class. `FormGroup` holds a `FormControl` per field.
The model always has the current values.
On submit read `form.value` and send it.
Angular Form Validation: Built-in and Cu: Validators are rules a control must satisfy: `required`, `minLength`, `email`.
Angular checks them on each change and sets the status.
Show an error only when the control is invalid and touched.
A custom validator is a function that returns an error object, or `null` when valid.
Angular Template-Driven Forms with ngMod: Template-driven form: most of the setup is in the HTML.
Add `ngModel` and a `name` to each input.
Use HTML attributes like `required` for validation.
FormControl, FormGroup, FormBuilder, set: `FormControl` = one field. `FormGroup` = a group of fields. `FormBuilder` = shorter way to create them.
`setValue` needs every field. `patchValue` updates only some.
`valueChanges` emits on each change. `statusChanges` emits when valid or invalid changes.
Unsubscribe or use `takeUntilDestroyed` when you listen manually.
Angular Forms: Select Dropdowns, Checkbo: Select and radio groups store one chosen value. A checkbox stores `true` or `false`.
Typed forms know the type of each control, so mistakes show in the editor.
`FormRecord` is for groups where the keys are not known in advance.
Angular Advanced Form Validation: Custom: Custom validators encode your rules, such as a password policy.
Async validators wait for a result (is the username taken?). The control is `pending` meanwhile.
A cross-field validator sits on the group and compares fields, like password and confirm.
`setValidators` changes rules at runtime. Then call `updateValueAndValidity()`.
Angular Routing Basics: Pages, RouterLin: Routing shows different pages for different URLs without a full reload.
Routes are listed in `app.routes.ts`: a `path` and a `component`.
`<router-outlet />` marks where the page is drawn.
Angular Route Parameters and Query Param: Route parameter: required part of the path, `/products/:id`.
Query parameter: optional, after the `?`, like `?sort=price&page=2`.
The component reads both and loads the right data.
`withComponentInputBinding()` lets route params arrive as inputs.
Angular Router Navigation: ActivatedRout: `routerLink` for links in a template. `router.navigate([...])` when code decides, for example after saving.
`ActivatedRoute` gives params, query params and route data.
Router events tell you when navigation starts and ends. Use them for loading bars.
Angular Route Guards: Protect Pages with: A guard is a function that decides whether a route may open: `canActivate: [authGuard]`.
Return `true` to open, or a redirect (`router.parseUrl('/login')`).
The server must still check permissions. A guard only hides pages.
Angular Guards: CanActivateChild, CanDea: `canActivateChild` protects all children of a route.
`canDeactivate` runs before leaving: warn about unsaved changes.
`resolve` fetches data before the page shows.
`canMatch` decides whether a route applies at all, for example by role.
Preloading can fetch lazy routes in the background.
Angular Lazy Loading: Load Routes and Co: Without lazy loading the first download holds the whole app.
A lazy route is split into its own file: `loadComponent: () => import('./page').then(m => m.Page)`.
The file downloads only when the user opens the route. `loadChildren` does it for a group of routes.
The first load stays small and fast.
Angular HttpClient: Get Data from an API: Keep API calls in a service, not in the component.
Add `provideHttpClient()` in the app config. Then `inject(HttpClient)`.
`http.get<T>(url)` returns an observable. Nothing is sent until someone subscribes.
Subscribe, or use the `async` pipe, and show the data.
Angular HTTP: Loading State, Error Handl: Set a loading flag before the request so the user sees something is happening.
`http.post(url, body)` sends data as the request body.
On success turn off loading and update the screen.
On failure catch the error and show a clear message, not a blank screen.
Angular HTTP: Query Parameters, Headers,: One service can cover every action your API supports.
`HttpParams` or `{ params: { page: 2 } }` for query parameters. Headers for tokens and content type.
PUT replaces a whole item. PATCH changes only some fields. DELETE removes an item by id.
Each call returns an observable of the result.
RxJS Basics for Angular: Observables and: An observable = a stream of values over time (clicks, HTTP results).
Operators are small steps added with `pipe()`: `map` changes each value, `filter` keeps some.
Unsubscribe when done, or let the `async` pipe do it.
RxJS Observables Explained: Create from: `of(1, 2, 3)` emits the values you give, then completes.
`from([..])` turns an array, string or promise into a stream.
`fromEvent(el, 'click')` turns browser events into a stream.
RxJS take, takeUntil, takeWhile, first,: `skip(n)` ignores the first values. `take(n)` stops after n values.
`tap` looks at values, for logging, without changing them.
`takeUntil(destroy$)` is a common way to clean up.
RxJS scan, reduce, debounceTime, debounc: `debounceTime(400)` waits until typing stops: one API call instead of one per key.
`scan` keeps a running result and emits it for every value, like a live total.
`reduce` emits only the final result, when the stream completes.
`delay` and `delayWhen` shift values later in time.
RxJS Error Handling: throwError, catchEr: An error ends an observable unless you handle it.
`retry(3)` tries again a set number of times.
`catchError` lets you recover: return a fallback with `of(...)`, or `throwError` to pass on a clearer error.
`finalize` runs at the end either way: a good place to hide a spinner.
RxJS Subjects in Angular: Subject, Behav: A subject is an observable you can also push values into with `next()`.
`BehaviorSubject` keeps the latest value, so new subscribers get it at once.
`AsyncSubject` gives only the last value, on completion.
Prefer signals for simple shared state in new code.
Test Angular Components and Services wit: A test: set up, do something, check the result.
`TestBed` creates the component with the same setup the app uses.
Change inputs or click a button, then let Angular update with `fixture.detectChanges()`.
Use `expect` to check text or values. Vitest runs the file.
For services, mock the HTTP calls.
Angular Accessibility: Build Apps Everyo: Accessibility = people with different needs can use your app.
Use the right HTML: real buttons, links, labels and headings.
ARIA only where plain HTML cannot say it.
Everything must work with the keyboard, with a visible focus.
Manage focus when the page changes so screen reader users know where they are.
Angular Performance and Production Build: A production build minifies and removes unused code: `ng build`.
Lazy loading keeps the first download small.
Check bundle sizes and measure with Lighthouse.
Angular Project 1: Build a Task Manager: Task manager: add form, list, toggle and delete, filter (all, active, done).
A service keeps all tasks in one signal.
A computed signal gives the filtered list.
Angular Project 2: Employee Management D: Employee dashboard: list, detail page and edit form.
A service talks to the API for all employee data.
The table page has search and sorting.
A reactive form with validators adds or edits an employee.
Routes connect the pages. A guard can protect the edit screens.
Angular Project 3: Online Learning Platf: Capstone: login with a guard, token sent with requests.
Courses load from an API on lazy routes.
A lesson page reads its id from the route.
Progress is kept in signals and saved back to the API.
Deploy an Angular App: Netlify, Firebase: `ng build` creates the production files in `dist`.
Upload `dist` to Netlify, Firebase Hosting or your own Nginx server.
The host must send `index.html` for unknown paths, or refreshing a deep link gives a 404.
Angular effect() and linkedSignal(): Adv: `linkedSignal` = a writable signal derived from another signal.
When the source changes it resets to a new default. You can still `set` it yourself.
`effect()` reruns when the signals it reads change.
Use effect for side effects, such as saving to storage. Not for computing values.
Angular resource() and httpResource(): S: `httpResource` loads data from an API and exposes it as signals.
It watches a request signal, such as an id, and sends a new request when it changes.
`resource()` works the same way for any async source.
Check the current docs, these APIs are newer and may change.
Angular Custom Directives: Attribute Dir: A directive adds behaviour to an existing element. It has no template.
The `host` property binds classes and styles and listens to events on that element.
Angular Content Projection: ng-content,: Content projection: a parent puts its own HTML inside a component.
The component marks a spot with `<ng-content />`.
The parent writes content between the component tags.
`ng-template` holds markup that is drawn only when `ngTemplateOutlet` renders it.
Angular Dynamic Components and Host Dire: Dynamic component = chosen at runtime, such as in a dialog.
Host directives let a component apply a directive's behaviour to itself, with no extra template code.
Angular ElementRef, Renderer2, HostBindi: `ElementRef` gives a handle on the element itself.
Prefer `Renderer2` to change it: safer and portable.
`@HostBinding` sets host properties. `@HostListener` listens for host events.
These decorators are the older style. Newer code uses the `host` metadata.
Angular Injection Tokens and Providers:: An injection token names a value that is not a class, such as a URL: `new InjectionToken<string>('API_URL')`.
A provider says which value the token gets: `{ provide: API_URL, useValue: '...' }`.
In tests, provide a different value or a fake class. The code does not change.
Angular HTTP Interceptors: Auth Tokens,: An interceptor sits between `HttpClient` and the network and sees every request and response.
Clone the request to add an auth token header.
Handle errors in one place, such as sending the user to login on a 401.
A counter in an interceptor can drive one global loading bar.
Angular Project Architecture: Features,: As an app grows, the folder layout matters more than any single file.
Group code by feature: orders, users, each with its own components and services.
`core` = app-wide services. `shared` = reusable components and pipes.
Features should not reach into each other. Share through core or shared.
Angular App Configuration, Environment V: Settings that differ between development and production go in configuration.
Provide them through `app.config.ts`, for example with an injection token.
`provideAppInitializer` runs a function before the app starts, such as loading remote settings.
Anything in a browser app is public. Never put secrets in it.
Angular Error Handling: Global ErrorHand: Provide a custom `ErrorHandler` to catch errors nobody else caught.
Send details to a logging service so you can fix them.
Show the user a short, friendly message, not a stack trace.
Handle expected HTTP errors close to the request. Let the global handler catch the rest.
Angular NgModules (Legacy), Module Routi: Older Angular apps group code into NgModules, with module routing and lazy modules.
New code uses standalone components that list their own `imports`.
Migration schematics convert modules to standalone step by step.
Angular Custom Form Controls with Contro: `ControlValueAccessor` lets your component act like a form input, for example a star rating.
`writeValue` receives the value from the form so the control can show it.
Call `onChange` to send a new value back. Call `onTouched` when touched.
The form then treats it like any other control, with validation.
Angular FormArray and Dynamic Forms: Add: A `FormArray` holds a list of controls, such as several phone numbers. It lives inside a `FormGroup`.
The template loops over the controls with `@for`.
Angular Signal Forms: Build Forms with S: Signal forms = a newer way to build forms based on signals.
Start with a signal holding your data as the model. The form is created from the model.
Each field exposes its state as signals: value, valid, touched.
This API is still evolving. Check the current docs before relying on it.
Angular State Management with a Signal S: A store = a service that keeps state in a private signal.
Components never change the state directly. They call methods on the store.
The store exposes read-only `computed` signals as selectors.
Views read the selectors and update automatically.
Advanced RxJS Patterns for Angular: Comb: `combineLatest` emits when any stream changes, with the latest value of each.
`switchMap` starts a request for that value and cancels the previous one if still running.
`share` or `shareReplay` lets many subscribers use one request.
Advanced Angular Routing: Resolvers, Chi: Child routes appear inside a layout's `<router-outlet />`.
A resolver fetches data before the page opens, so it never shows empty.
Preloading downloads lazy routes in the background after the first load.
View transitions can animate between pages when the browser supports it.
Angular Change Detection and Zoneless Ap: Change detection = how Angular finds out what to update on screen.
With zone.js, Angular is told after any async task and then checks components.
Signals tell Angular exactly which view depends on what, so less work is needed.
Zoneless apps do not need zone.js: signals and events trigger updates.
`OnPush` checks a component only when its inputs, events or signals change.
Angular Server-Side Rendering (SSR) and: A normal Angular app sends an almost empty page and builds the content in the browser.
SSR: the server runs Angular and sends full HTML, so people and search engines see content at once.
Hydration attaches Angular to the existing HTML so it becomes interactive without redrawing.
Angular SEO: Title, Meta Tags, Canonical: Set a unique title for every route with the `Title` service.
Use the `Meta` service for the description, and a canonical link.
SSR puts all of this in the HTML crawlers receive.
Lazy-load images below the fold and give them sizes.
Advanced Angular Testing: Guards, Interc: Test a guard with `runInInjectionContext` and check what it returns.
Test an interceptor with `HttpTestingController`: see the request, send a fake response.
The router testing harness navigates and lets you check which component showed.
Angular End-to-End Testing with Playwrig: An end-to-end test uses your app the way a user does.
Playwright opens a real browser, clicks and types, finding things by role and label.
Then it checks what appears on the screen.
Keep a few tests for the most important journeys: sign-up, checkout.
Angular Security Best Practices: XSS, To: Angular escapes values in templates, which protects against XSS. Avoid `bypassSecurityTrust...` unless you really must.
HttpOnly cookies are safer than local storage for tokens, but cookies need CSRF protection.
Set security headers such as `Content-Security-Policy` on your server.
The server must check every request.
Angular CI/CD with GitHub Actions: Test,: CI/CD runs your checks and deployment for you, every time.
A push starts the workflow: install, lint, test, build, deploy.
If a step fails, the later steps do not run.
Keep secrets in GitHub secrets, never in the repository.
Angular Troubleshooting: 404 on Refresh,: 404 on refresh: the server does not know Angular routes. Send `index.html` for unknown paths.
`ExpressionChangedAfterItHasBeenChecked`: a value changed after Angular checked it. Move the change earlier or use signals.
`EventTarget` typing errors: cast to the element you expect.
SSL on localhost: create and trust a local certificate for the dev server.
Read the error message, find the cause, fix that.
Angular Module Loaders: SystemJS, Webpac: A bundler turns many source files into files a browser can load.
Early Angular used SystemJS, then Webpack for many years.
Modern Angular builds with esbuild, and the dev server uses Vite. Both are much faster.
You still run `ng build` and `ng serve`.
Angular Advanced Capstone: Build and Shi: Plan the architecture first: features, routes, clear boundaries.
Add state with signals and load data over HTTP, with errors handled.
Test it. Check accessibility and security.
Add SSR and performance work. Let CI/CD ship it.
